parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$y=3+2\sin\frac14x$, leading to $\sin\frac14x=\frac{y-3}{2}$ — M1; attempt to isolate $\sin(\frac14x)$. Condone sign errors. Variables may be interchanged initially. M1 is not implied by an unsupported inverse-sine expression.
$x=4\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{y-3}{2}\right)$, leading to $f^{-1}(x)=4\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x-3}{2}\right)$ — A1; must clearly be $\sin^{-1}((x-3)/2)$, not $\frac12\sin^{-1}(x-3)$. Allow division by $\frac14$ expressed equivalently, but not multiplication by $\frac14$.
Total: 2

parts.answer: Yes; the completed graph is strictly increasing, so $g$ is one-to-one.

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: Stretch by factor $4$ in the $x$-direction, stretch by factor $2$ in the $y$-direction, then translate by $\binom{0}{3}$; the translation must follow the vertical stretch.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Stretch by factor 4 in the $x$-direction — B2,1,0; B2 fully correct, B1 with two of the three elements correct. Condone “sf”, stretched coordinates, horizontal stretch, $y$-axis invariant, or wavelength/period increased by factor 4 for full credit as specified.
Stretch by factor 2 in the $y$-direction — B2,1,0; B2 fully correct, B1 with two elements correct. Condone “sf”, vertical stretch, $x$-axis invariant, doubled $y$-coordinates or doubled amplitude as specified.
Translation by $\binom03$ — B2,1,0; B2 fully correct, B1 with two elements correct. Allow “shift”. Mention of the $y$-axis, $y$-direction or vertically supplies the zero horizontal component. “Shift by 3 vertically” is B2, but “shift by a factor of 3” or “translation of 3 up” is B1.
After B2,B2, the final transformation earns B2 only if the order is fully correct: the translation must not precede the $y$-stretch. If all else is correct but the order is wrong, award B2B2B1.
Total: 6
